source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.6
text: Beyond raw milled rice, rice can be processed into 'secondary products' at different levels of readiness for consumption, which is a useful way to think about product diversification for market. Two main categories are described: (1) Partly cooked rice products, which must be heated before serving — examples shown include packaged rice noodle/vermicelli bundles sold in retail plastic packaging; and (2) Ready-to-eat rice products, which only need to be warmed before serving or can be served directly — examples include rice-based cookies (some appearing to contain black sesame and herbs), and rice-based gift-basket assortments combining packaged rice, rice cookies, and other rice snack products wrapped for retail or gift sale. This distinction (partly cooked vs. ready-to-eat) is a simple framework a rice processor or seller can use to position products for convenience-focused buyers.
